title: From Recall to Reasoning: Automated Question Generation for Deeper Math Learning through Large Language Models
extended_summary:
This paper investigates how large language models can be used to generate higher-quality mathematics practice questions that support deeper learning rather than simple recall. The authors focus on two research questions: whether providing more contextual information improves the quality and cognitive depth of AI-generated questions, and how an LLM-based system can be designed to generate math questions at different levels of cognitive complexity. The broader motivation is to help educators use generative AI effectively for content creation while addressing concerns about relevance, quality, and pedagogical alignment.

The paper reports two connected empirical studies. In Study 1, the authors tested Gemini-1.5-Pro in a mathematical logic course by prompting it to generate five comprehension questions under three context conditions: minimal, moderate, and comprehensive. Outputs were evaluated by a logic-knowledgeable math student on relevance, Bloom's Taxonomy depth, and answer correctness. In Study 2, the authors developed QG-DOK, a framework that combines retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with Webb's Depth of Knowledge (DOK) levels. They embedded mathematical materials in a vector database and used retrieved examples plus DOK-level prompting to guide generation. They then compared DOK-only prompting against DOK+RAG across GPT-4o, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemini-1.5-Pro using automated metrics for relevance, DOK alignment, appropriateness, and lexical diversity.

The context is advanced mathematics in higher education, specifically a mathematical logic course at McGill University in Canada. The work is framed around supporting educator workflows and improving student learning materials rather than testing student learning outcomes directly. Users discussed in the paper include educators creating questions and students who would use the resulting practice problems; evaluation was conducted primarily on generated content rather than on classroom performance.

The main conclusions are that LLMs can generate relevant and sometimes high-quality math questions with minimal support, but simply adding more raw context does not reliably improve relevance and may introduce hallucinated content. The proposed DOK+RAG framework improved relevance and appropriateness over DOK-only prompting, especially for higher-order questions, suggesting that grounding generation in retrieved instructional materials is useful for producing deeper and more context-aware math questions. However, the paper also notes continuing challenges with mid-level cognitive depth alignment, mathematical notation handling, limited evaluation data, and the preliminary nature of the findings.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google family large language model used for generative text production.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in Study 1 as the sole LLM (Gemini-1.5-Pro) to generate five advanced math comprehension questions and answers under three prompt-context conditions: minimal, moderate, and comprehensive course context.

findings.finding_summary: In Study 1, Gemini-generated question relevance was perfect under minimal and moderate context but declined under comprehensive context, while answer correctness improved with more context. Mean relevance was 1.00 ± 0.00 (minimal), 1.00 ± 0.00 (moderate), and 0.80 ± 0.45 (comprehensive); mean correctness was 0.60 ± 0.55, 0.80 ± 0.45, and 1.00 ± 0.00 respectively. Depth remained relatively constant across conditions at 2.60 ± 1.14, 2.60 ± 1.82, and 2.40 ± 2.07.
findings.measure: Human-evaluated relevance (binary), cognitive depth (0-6 Bloom's Taxonomy score), and correctness (binary) of generated math questions/answers across three context scenarios

findings.finding_summary: In Study 2, Gemini performed better with DOK+RAG than with DOK-only on average for relevance, DOK alignment, and appropriateness in math question generation, though gains varied by level. Average scores were relevance 0.73 to 0.75, DOK alignment 0.56 to 0.70, and appropriateness 0.82 to 0.91; at Level 4, relevance improved from 0.63 to 0.73 while DOK alignment increased from 0.46 to 0.58.
findings.measure: G-Eval scores for relevance, DOK alignment, and appropriateness; PINC lexical diversity for generated math questions

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI GPT-family large language model used for generative text production.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in Study 2 as GPT-4o within the QG-DOK comparison to generate math questions under DOK-only prompting versus DOK+RAG prompting.

findings.finding_summary: For GPT-4o, DOK+RAG matched or exceeded DOK-only on most metrics, with notable gains in higher-order question generation and appropriateness. Average scores were relevance 0.81 vs 0.81, DOK alignment 0.48 vs 0.71, and appropriateness 0.90 vs 0.92; at Level 4, DOK alignment improved from 0.29 to 0.61 and appropriateness from 0.82 to 0.90.
findings.measure: G-Eval scores for relevance, DOK alignment, and appropriateness; PINC lexical diversity for generated math questions

identified_tools.name: DeepSeek
identified_tools.description: DeepSeek family large language model used for generative text production.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in Study 2 as DeepSeek-V3 within the QG-DOK comparison to generate math questions under DOK-only prompting versus DOK+RAG prompting.

findings.finding_summary: For DeepSeek-V3, DOK+RAG generally improved math question generation quality over DOK-only, especially on relevance and higher-level depth alignment. Average scores were relevance 0.77 to 0.79, DOK alignment 0.64 to 0.69, and appropriateness 0.86 to 0.92; at Level 4, relevance increased from 0.66 to 0.71 and DOK alignment from 0.39 to 0.59.
findings.measure: G-Eval scores for relevance, DOK alignment, and appropriateness; PINC lexical diversity for generated math questions

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / LLM-based automated question generation system for producing math practice problems.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied broadly as an automated math question-generation approach, including the proposed QG-DOK framework that combines retrieval-augmented generation with Webb's Depth of Knowledge to generate context-aware questions at varying cognitive levels.

findings.finding_summary: Across the paper's two studies, the authors report that generative AI can create math problems of varying quality with minimal support, and that providing examples plus relevant content improves output quality. The proposed DOK+RAG framework consistently outperformed DOK-only prompting across tested LLMs, particularly for higher-order thinking levels (DOK 3 and 4), while average PINC scores around 0.92 suggested strong lexical diversity.
findings.measure: Human evaluation and G-Eval of generated question relevance, correctness, cognitive depth/DOK alignment, appropriateness, and PINC lexical diversity

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory empirical paper with two small-scope evaluation studies, relying on prompt comparisons, automated scoring, and a single human evaluator rather than an RCT or strong quasi-experimental design. Sample sizes and inferential statistics are not reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports improvements in evaluation metrics for question-generation quality, especially with DOK+RAG, but no standardized effect sizes or student learning outcome impacts are provided. Impact is promising but unclear and operational rather than directly causal on learner achievement.
